chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from his father, from Abu al-Jahm, from Abu Khadijah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The offspring of fornication is never pure, nor is its price pure, and the Mimmzir is not pure for seven generations.'
It was asked, 'What is the Mimmzir?' He said, 'The man who earns wealth from what is not permissible to him, then marries or takes a concubine, and a child is born to him; that child is the Mimmzir.'

key_terms.الْمِمْزِيرُ: The Mimmzir (one who mixes lawful with unlawful)
key_terms.ثَمَنُهُ: Its price/value (referring to the wealth used)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Mimmzir and its ruling on impurity in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of *Mimmzir*—an individual whose lineage is spiritually tainted because he acquired wealth through unlawful means (*ghayr hilihi*) to marry or take a concubine. This impurity (*la yatibu*) extends not only to the offspring of such unions but also to the wealth itself, with the spiritual consequence persisting for seven generations, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the purity of both source and result in familial and economic transactions.
